draft.emotion: everyday and practical, picking them up to start a meal
notes: Often used with the polite prefix お (お箸). Counted in pairs with 膳 (zen), as in 一膳 (ichizen).
Distinguished in speech from 橋 (hashi, 'bridge') and 端 (hashi, 'edge') by pitch accent: 箸 starts high (HA-shi) in standard Tokyo Japanese.

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks held in one hand and used for eating food.
